_comment: Generate and animate a configurable four-direction character, then package it for RPG Maker XP, VX, VX Ace, MV, or MZ. The version is an export-profile selector only; MZ and its conventional 48x48 cell are the defaults.
_comment_prompt: /pixellab-pip create an RPG Maker character spritesheet with RPG Maker version, character, and character cell size variables; default to MZ, its conventional cell size, and an adult male human chibi base character with non-explicit doll-like anatomy and no clothing or equipment

TASK.instruction: Before any PixelLab call, require an explicit current-user request to run this blueprint and confirm callable PixelLab MCP create_character, get_character, and animate_character tools are visible. If PixelLab MCP is unavailable or unconfigured, stop before spending and show the setup link https://www.pixellab.ai/mcp; do not silently substitute a REST call. Resolve output_directory by using the declared path when available or appending the lowest available suffix starting at -2. Resolve {{RPG Maker version | default: MZ}} case-insensitively as a packaging-profile enum with exactly one value: XP, VX, VX Ace/VXAce, MV, or MZ. Reject unsupported versions and ambiguous names instead of guessing. Never insert this export-profile value into a PixelLab image description. Resolve {{character cell size | default: engine conventional}} to target cell width CW and height CH. When the value is `engine conventional` case-insensitively, map the resolved version to primitive dimensions exactly: XP=32x48, VX=32x32, VX Ace/VXAce=32x32, MV=48x48, MZ=48x48. An explicit override may be one positive integer N or `Npx` for an NxN cell, or two positive integers written `WIDTHxHEIGHT` optionally followed by `px`; reject every other form instead of inferring it. This dependency mapping belongs to this TASK; do not rewrite the blueprint or treat PixelLab's create_character size as the RPG Maker cell size. Character cell size controls only the exported RPG Maker cell canvas; it does not change create_character.size. An override larger than the native subject bounds adds transparent padding because this workflow never upscales. A larger generated subject requires a separate current-request override of the PixelLab generation size and full revalidation before spending. Create the resolved directory empty. Read the auto setting once immediately before spending. The paid plan has two MCP calls: (1) create_character in standard mode for approximately 1 generation, listing the fully resolved description plus body_type, detail, n_directions, outline, proportions, shading, size, text_guidance_scale, and view; (2) animate_character in template mode for approximately 4 generations total, listing template_animation_id=walking-4-frames, animation_name=RPG Maker walk source, directions=[south, west, east, north], and ai_freedom=0. With auto off, render the exact auto.md framing: `💳 **Approve this PixelLab run?** — **~5 generations** *(or credits)*.`, the two numbered call blocks, `Reply **yes / no**, or say what to **change**.`, and `*Tip: reply `auto` (or `/pixellab-pip auto`) to run future jobs without this check.*`; wait for approval. With auto on, render `⚡ **Auto is on — running PixelLab job(s)** — **~5 generations** *(or credits)*.`, the same two call blocks, and `*Disable auto with `/pixellab-pip auto`.*`, then continue without pausing. Stop before spending if any precondition or required approval fails.
TASK.verify: Current-user run authority and PixelLab MCP availability are confirmed; the version resolves to one verified profile; character cell size resolves to positive integer CW and CH using either the exact profile mapping or a valid explicit override; the output directory is new, empty, writable, and inside the current project; and the full paid chain was disclosed and approved according to the active auto-approval setting.

MCP create_character.description: {{character | default: adult male human chibi base character, non-explicit doll-like anatomy, no clothing or equipment}}, readable four-direction top-down map sprite, clean silhouette, consistent identity and proportions, flat pixel art, limited palette, hard edges

TASK.instruction: Use the fresh character ID returned by the immediately preceding create_character call with PixelLab get_character. Poll without resubmitting until completed or failed. Save the completed rotations unchanged as candidates/01/rotations/south.png, candidates/01/rotations/west.png, candidates/01/rotations/east.png, and candidates/01/rotations/north.png. Decode and record the actual returned canvas width and height; PixelLab's requested size=48 describes the character, and a larger transparently padded source canvas is expected rather than an error. Require all four rotations to have identical actual dimensions and preserve every pixel and alpha value. Build candidates/01/contact-sheet.png as a separate labeled review aid without altering the saved rotations. Do not start animation yet. For each regeneration, allocate the next unused two-digit candidate directory (02, 03, and so on) and never overwrite an earlier candidate.
TASK.verify: Exactly four readable transparent rotations exist with one identical observed canvas size, their direction labels resolve unambiguously to south, west, east, and north, and the contact sheet displays the same pixels. The observed source canvas may be larger than 48x48 and is recorded as an observation, not used as the RPG Maker cell size or replay requirement.

TASK.instruction:
Display the four-direction contact sheet and render this checkpoint exactly as a readable Markdown choice: `🎭 **Character ready — choose the next step**

1. **Continue animating** — create the engine-appropriate walk frames for all four directions.
2. **Regenerate character** — describe what to change; this adds another paid character generation and will be cost-gated.
3. **Stop here** — keep the four directional base sprites without creating an animated engine sheet.

Reply **1 / 2 / 3**, or describe the changes you want.` Wait for the user's choice. On Continue, proceed to the animation TASK; the four animation jobs were already included in the approved chain, so do not ask for a second spend approval. On Regenerate, collect the requested changes, disclose and cost-gate one additional create_character call under the active auto-approval setting, never delete or overwrite the prior character, submit the revised description with every other create_character field unchanged, poll the replacement's fresh ID, save and show its four rotations, then repeat this checkpoint. If the paid plan or material inputs change beyond that disclosed extra creation, re-plan and re-approve before spending. On Stop, make no animation call and stop successfully after reporting the saved rotation files are not an engine-ready animated sheet.
TASK.verify: No animation starts before an explicit Continue choice; every regeneration receives its own paid-call disclosure or auto-approval record and uses a fresh ID; Stop incurs no later paid calls.

TASK.instruction: Execute only after the checkpoint's Continue choice. Copy the current reviewed candidate's rotations unchanged to approved/rotations/south.png, approved/rotations/west.png, approved/rotations/east.png, and approved/rotations/north.png. Call PixelLab animate_character once for the currently approved fresh character ID with mode=template, template_animation_id=walking-4-frames, animation_name=RPG Maker walk source, directions=[south, west, east, north], and ai_freedom=0. This queues the four paid directional jobs already disclosed in the initial plan. Poll get_character until all four animations complete or one fails; never retry automatically. Save every returned frame unchanged and in returned order as approved/walk/<direction>/01.png through 04.png. Decode and record every returned frame's actual canvas dimensions. Require all 16 animation frames to share one canvas size and require that size to match the approved rotations; stop before packaging if either check fails. A common padded canvas larger than the requested character size is valid and must remain unchanged in these source files. For each direction, create approved/walk/<direction>/source-order-preview.gif as a separate looping preview with a non-undefined disposal method.
TASK.verify: The current reviewed character has four ordered four-frame directional walk animations; all approved rotations and all 16 walk frames share one recorded source canvas size even when that canvas is larger than 48x48; and every animation is labeled south, west, east, or north. Each source-order preview has four frames in the same order, loops, uses an explicit disposal method, and coalesces back to the source frames without unexpected pixel differences.

TASK.instruction: Execute only after successful animation. Package the approved PixelLab pixels for the resolved {{RPG Maker version | default: MZ}} profile without repainting. Use target cell width CW and height CH already derived during preflight from {{character cell size | default: engine conventional}}; if execution state was not retained, repeat the exact mapping and override parser from that preflight TASK before packaging. PixelLab's create_character size=48 is a subject-size request, and the observed padded source canvas is never a target cell or sheet dimension. Map PixelLab directions to rows exactly: south is row 1 (Down), west is row 2 (Left), east is row 3 (Right), and north is row 4 (Up). For every direction, compute one union bounding box of every pixel with alpha greater than zero across all poses used in that row, and stop if any pose has no such pixel. Crop the same union rectangle from every pose in that row. Let maxW be the maximum nonzero-alpha union width across all four rows and maxH be the maximum union height. Set the shared scale to min(1, CW/maxW, CH/maxH) and apply that identical nearest-neighbor scale to every delivered pose. Preserve aspect ratio, keep a shared horizontal center and bottom/foot baseline within each row, and add only transparent padding to make every delivered cell exactly CWxCH. Never fit frames independently, never crop any pixel whose alpha is greater than zero, and never carry PixelLab's extra source-canvas padding into the target cell merely because it was returned. For XP, create a transparent PNG named rpg-maker-character.png with 4 columns by 4 rows, exactly 4*CW pixels wide by 4*CH pixels high; columns 1, 2, 3, and 4 are PixelLab walk frames 1, 2, 3, and 4 in unchanged returned order, matching XP playback 1→2→3→4. Do not insert the static rotation into XP's four animation columns. Create rpg-maker-character-engine-playback.gif as a four-row preview that animates all direction rows in parallel using 1→2→3→4 and visually verify the 4→1 seam; stop if the gait is not a clean cycle. For VX/VX Ace/MV/MZ, create a transparent PNG named $rpg-maker-character.png with 3 columns by 4 rows, exactly 3*CW pixels wide by 4*CH pixels high. In every VX/VX Ace/MV/MZ row, column 1 is the earlier of two visually verified opposing stride poses selected from the four returned frames, column 2 is that direction's reviewed static rotation/standing pose, and column 3 is the later opposing stride pose; this matches engine playback 2→1→2→3. Preserve chronological order between the selected stride poses. Create rpg-maker-character-engine-playback.gif as a four-row preview that animates all direction rows in parallel using 2→1→2→3. If two opposing stride poses cannot be verified, either selected stride is a duplicate, or the standing pose visibly jumps against the walk frames for any direction, stop instead of guessing or fabricating a frame. Create a separate rpg-maker-character-inspection-grid.png with the exact CWxCH cell boundaries and label it `Inspection aid — expected grid overlay`; never alter the delivered sheet.
TASK.verify: The original delivered PNG, engine-order playback preview, and separate inspection grid all decode. Every delivered cell is exactly the resolved positive-integer CWxCH and the sheet is exactly 4*CW by 4*CH for XP or 3*CW by 4*CH for VX/VX Ace/MV/MZ. With `engine conventional`, those dimensions resolve exactly to XP 32x48 cells and a 128x192 sheet, VX/VX Ace 32x32 cells and a 96x128 sheet, or MV/MZ 48x48 cells and a 144x192 sheet. XP maps rows Down/Left/Right/Up, maps columns to returned frames 1/2/3/4, and loops cleanly across 4→1. VX/VX Ace/MV/MZ use a leading `$`, map rows Down/Left/Right/Up, and have movement/standing/movement in columns 1/2/3 with opposing stride phases. The engine-order preview uses the target engine's actual column sequence and shows no scale, center, foot-baseline, or standing-pose jitter. Every source direction appears in exactly one correct row; every pixel with alpha greater than zero stays inside its cell; all poses use the one computed global scale; no pose is upscaled or repainted; PixelLab's observed padded canvas does not change CW, CH, or the computed sheet dimensions; transparent padding remains transparent; and the inspection grid is not treated as proof of content alignment.
